osmTags.inscription: It is said that Henry Tudor (later King Henry VII) escaped through a tunnel here in 1471 when he escaped to France
East Rock House. Admiral Lord Nelson, Sir William and Lady Hamilton stayed here in 1802
Nina Hamnett 1890‒1956 Artist was born here on St. Valentine’s Day
Kenneth Griffith actor and film maker born here 12th October 1921

Eric Bradforth
1920‒2012
artist/designer and long-time resident of Tenby
lived and worked here
Gwilym Prichard 1931‒2015 the eminent Welsh artist lived and worked here in later life with his wife, fellow artist Claudia Williams
The ‘Five Arches’ was the south west gate into the town. It is the logo of the Walled Towns Friendship Circle founded in 1991
The site of the Sea Water Baths and Assembly Rooms built by Sir William Paxton in 1811. “The sea washes away all the ills of men” (Euripides)
Tenby House built in 1821 by Sir William Paxton on the site of the Globe Inn. John Wesley preached from the Old Market Cross nearby in 1763 and 1784
This Archway formerly gave entrance to the Churchyard, Town Hall and Gaol
Charles Norris 1779‒1858 artist-author of “Etchings of Tenby,” 1812 lived here c.1805‒1821
While on holiday here Mary Ann Evans was inspired to write her first novel published in 1857 under the name of George Eliot
These arches and walls were preserved to the town by an invocation of the Court of Chancery obtained June 23rd in the year 1873 by the late George Chater FRCS

Post Brenhinol Royal Mail
This Victorian pillar box is dedicated to the memory of
Mr. H. H. B. Lee
Last Head Postmaster of Tenby 1959‒1964
Mayor of Tenby 1971‒1972 and local historian
Dedicated 4 May 1990
Roald Dahl children’s author stayed here in The Cabin every Easter Holiday between 1920‒36 with his Mother and siblings
1940 Headquarters of the First Belgian Fusiliers Battalion formed in Tenby which became The Belgian Liberation Brigade

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Location and terrain only. OpenStreetMap has no mapped outline for this site.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
